main_claim: Character-level seq2seq normalizes Amharic non-standard words with 94.8% accuracy.
evidence: Single reported accuracy of 94.8%; data and baselines not described.
rationale: Neutral title. Number reported but hedged as 'promising given the resource'; torn between 1 and 2, chose lower.

main_claim: SEARNN's global-local losses improve RNN training over MLE.
evidence: OCR and spelling correction; machine translation via subsampling strategy.
rationale: Neutral NAME: description title. Improvements scoped to named tasks.

main_claim: code2seq's AST-path encoding significantly outperforms code-specific models and state-of-the-art NMT models.
evidence: Two tasks, two programming languages, four datasets up to 16M examples; no numbers.
rationale: 'Significantly outperforms previous models' is strong language, but evaluation scope is stated; unquantified intensifier alone not treated as overreach (rule 1).

main_claim: Transformer-tracker attention modules are strong matchers for class-agnostic counting, achieving new state of the art.
evidence: MixFormer and TransT adaptations; FSC-147 and CARPK; ablation studies.
rationale: Claim title supported on named datasets. 'Count Everything' prefix is broad but names the task; torn, chose lower.

main_claim: Architecture matters for scaling; the best-performing architecture changes across scales.
evidence: Systematic study of ten architectures, upstream pretraining and downstream transfer.
rationale: Question title answered by abstract. Findings scoped to ten architectures; implications hedged with 'we believe'.

main_claim: IRIS, a Transformer world-model agent, sets state of the art on Atari 100k without lookahead search.
evidence: Atari 100k: mean human-normalized score 1.046; beats humans on 10 of 26 games.
rationale: Title generalises to 'Transformers' broadly from one agent on one benchmark; abstract claim precisely scoped with numbers.

main_claim: FOND achieves state-of-the-art DG for domain-linked classes, given enough domain-shared classes.
evidence: Experiments across popular DG tasks (unnamed); theoretical insights.
rationale: Neutral title. SOTA claim explicitly conditioned; introducing the task is a specific, not sweeping, novelty claim.

main_claim: Tree-structured VAE matches autoregressive log likelihood with fewer sequential computations.
evidence: One synthetic dataset and one automated theorem-proving dataset.
rationale: Neutral title. Modest, scoped parity claim stays within evidence.

main_claim: GLOBE-CE gives efficient, reliable global counterfactual explanations, fixing AReS scalability issues.
evidence: Real-world datasets and user studies; mathematical analysis of categorical feature translations.
rationale: Title asserts a reliability-efficiency impossibility; abstract gives no such result and claims its method improves both. Torn mild/clear, chose lower.

main_claim: NNGeometry offers a simple PyTorch interface for FIM and NTK linear algebra operations.
evidence: Library description, design motivation, demonstration on actual deep networks; no speed measurements.
rationale: 'Easy and Fast' attributes; speed not evidenced but abstract cites efficient approximations; torn, chose none. Abstract mainly descriptive.

main_claim: MaskCLR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art skeletal action recognition on standard and perturbed skeletons.
evidence: NTU60, NTU120, Kinetics400; single encoder (ST-MHSA); perturbations and different pose estimators.
rationale: SOTA on named benchmarks fine; 'seamlessly incorporated into transformer-based models' rests on one encoder; semantic-capture mechanism asserted without stated evidence.

main_claim: STAR gated cell preserves gradient magnitude, enabling substantially deeper RNNs with improved performance.
evidence: Gradient propagation analysis; five sequence modelling tasks on three datasets.
rationale: 'RNNs That Can Be Trained' read as attribute in noun phrase; supported. 'Substantially' unquantified but within stated tasks.

main_claim: GAM-SHAP variational link explains recent SHAP work; InstaSHAP computes Shapley values in one forward pass.
evidence: Theoretical connection and representation-power results; no empirical evaluation described.
rationale: Title supported by single-pass method. 'Deep insights into nearly all recent developments' is sweeping with no described support.

main_claim: Multi-task MLM/TLM on clusters of similar African languages strongly improves within-cluster translation.
evidence: New parallel dataset; similarity metric; +29 BLEU on Bafia-Ewondo versus non-multilingual prior methods.
rationale: Tentative 'On the use' title. 'For African Languages' broader than one cluster, but framing tentative; torn, chose none.

main_claim: Contrastive pre-training yields retrievers competitive with BM25 unsupervised and SOTA on BEIR after fine-tuning.
evidence: Many domains versus BM25; few-shot versus BERT; BEIR after MS-MARCO fine-tuning.
rationale: Neutral title. SOTA on a named benchmark (rule 2); 'competitive' is modest.

main_claim: Pixel-wise ablation weights produce better CAM explanations than channel-wise weights.
evidence: Unspecified experiments; authors' own adversarial-attack-based evaluation metrics.
rationale: Prescriptive title coded 2. 'Superiority' unscoped and evidence undetailed, but missing detail alone is not overreach (rule 1).

main_claim: Learned divisive normalization improves AlexNet recognition by 1-2 points and alters internal representations.
evidence: AlexNet on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet; combined with batch, group, layer norm; manifold, sparsity, RF analyses.
rationale: Title scoped to AlexNet and supported. 'Always' refers to tested configurations with numbers; 'in doing so' only slightly causal.

main_claim: BagNets, a bag-of-local-features ResNet variant, reach high ImageNet accuracy and behave like SOTA DNNs.
evidence: 87.6% top-5 with 32px features; AlexNet-level with 16px; comparisons with VGG-16, ResNet-152, DenseNet-169.
rationale: Title scoped to ImageNet and supported. Hedged but broad inference that DNN progress is 'mostly' fine-tuning exceeds the comparison.

main_claim: Constraining unsupported flows in offline GFlowNets produces high-scoring, diverse candidates.
evidence: Experiments on 'several widely-used datasets' (unnamed).
rationale: Title verb claim ('Enable') supported by reported effectiveness. Abstract claims modest and scoped.

main_claim: Goal/framing disentanglement in LLM activations yields SOTA PAIR jailbreak detection and effective defense against adversarial prompts.
evidence: PAIR+Framing dataset; various LLM families; up to 21-point accuracy gain; theoretical separation guarantees.
rationale: Absolute 'Can't hide' title and conclusion about adversarial prompts generally extend beyond PAIR-only detection evaluation.

main_claim: Beam search degrades with width due to early, highly non-greedy decisions; constraining them removes degradation.
evidence: Empirical study on three sequence synthesis tasks; two constrained search methods.
rationale: General title supported by three-task analysis. 'Effectively eliminates the problem' strong but scoped; torn, chose lower.

main_claim: Reblurring losses exploiting the inverse task improve perceptual quality of deblurred images.
evidence: Large-scale benchmarks and real images; NIQE, LPIPS and visual sharpness.
rationale: Title premise stated as design intuition, consistent with abstract. Claims scoped to stated metrics.

main_claim: FL for ASR gives near-optimal models; FL with DP achieves user-level DP with small WER loss.
evidence: Large transformer ASR; (7.2, 1e-9)-DP with 1.3% WER drop, extrapolated to high population scale.
rationale: Neutral title. Numbers given and extrapolation disclosed; 'first baselines' qualified by 'not aware of prior work'.

main_claim: Complementary modality information improves VLM answers and reasoning; contradictory information harms performance and confidence.
evidence: SI-VQA dataset; benchmark of several VLMs including PaliGemma and LLaVA; accuracy, uncertainty, attention analyses.
rationale: 'Why context matters' is an implicit claim the findings support. Results scoped to tested VLMs.

main_claim: Fairness-enhancing MEDL boosts fairness across sensitive variables while preserving performance on clustered data.
evidence: Three datasets (two census/finance, one healthcare); fairness up to 82%, 43%, 86%, 27%.
rationale: Title claims in- and out-of-distribution gains; abstract reports no OOD evaluation. Abstract claims quantified; 'agnostic' framed as design property.

main_claim: FCVL improves single-source generalization of BEV 3D detection, achieving best performance across test domains.
evidence: Experiments on 'various testing domains' (unnamed); theoretical guarantees via augmentation graph theory.
rationale: 'Generalizable' attribute supported. 'Best performance' scoped to single-source setting; 'first' qualified by 'to the best of our knowledge'.

main_claim: Gaussian-smoothed Q-values satisfy a Bellman equation and enable Gaussian policy learning with strong results.
evidence: Theoretical derivations (Bellman equation, gradient/Hessian relations); standard continuous control benchmarks.
rationale: Neutral title. 'Strong results on standard benchmarks' is modest and scoped.

main_claim: Dual VQ codebooks in graph contrastive learning yield more robust, discriminative node representations.
evidence: No results reported; authors 'plan to demonstrate' competitive performance; mechanism only posited.
rationale: Title asserts superiority with no reported evidence. Abstract lists 'empirical validation' as a contribution while experiments are only planned.

main_claim: SAP learns task-agnostic priors from imperfect off-policy data and plans zero-shot, outperforming baselines.
evidence: Gridworld, robotics tasks and video games; comparisons with unnamed baseline methods.
rationale: 'Arbitrary quality interactions' and generalizable policy to unseen tasks are broader than the described evaluation.

main_claim: Fine-tuning an LLM to follow annotation guidelines improves zero-shot IE over previous attempts.
evidence: 'Comprehensive evaluation' with unnamed benchmarks; ablation showing detailed guidelines matter.
rationale: Title claim supported by abstract. Comparison not universal; 'previous attempts failed' concerns prior work, not own evidence.

main_claim: VLMs behave like bags-of-words; retrieval shortcuts likely explain it; composition-aware hard negatives help.
evidence: ARO benchmark (>50,000 cases); retrieval-without-order experiments; contrastive learning modification.
rationale: Question title addressed. Causal explanation hedged ('hypothesize'); 'significantly improves' unquantified but scoped to order/compositionality tasks.

main_claim: LLMs show surprisingly high but imperfect retrieval robustness, limiting full RAG benefits.
evidence: 1500-question benchmark; 11 LLMs; 3 prompting strategies; three robustness metrics.
rationale: Neutral title. Findings explicitly scoped to tested LLMs and benchmark.

main_claim: Exploiting laziness and Jacobian low-rankness enables scalable backpropagation-free training of over-parameterized models.
evidence: Unspecified empirical results 'confirm scalability and effectiveness'; no datasets or numbers.
rationale: Descriptive title. Definite but unscoped claim coded 2; 'new pathways' is forward-looking, not an overreaching result.

main_claim: Joint streaming/full-context training improves streaming ASR latency and accuracy, reaching state of the art.
evidence: ContextNet and Conformer on LibriSpeech and MultiDomain; ablations.
rationale: Title verb phrase describes method aim; supported. SOTA explicitly on named datasets (rule 2).

main_claim: Learning from reversals with differentiable physics and imitation learning enables superior rigid and deformable insertion.
evidence: Unspecified evaluations of sample efficiency, performance, sim-to-real; simulator-generated dataset.
rationale: 'Pioneers a paradigm shift' and unscoped 'superiority over competing approaches' exceed the vaguely described evaluations.

main_claim: Spatiotemporal contrastive learning on street view imagery significantly outperforms supervised and unsupervised methods on urban tasks.
evidence: Visual place recognition, socioeconomic estimation, perception tasks; no numbers or datasets named.
rationale: Generic 'Are Natural Learners' title supported across several tasks. Strong 'significantly outperforms' wording, but within listed tasks.

main_claim: Feature selection is largely insignificant: tiny random feature subsets match or beat full and published sets.
evidence: 30 datasets (RNA-Seq, mass spectrometry, imaging); random subsets match or outperform in 27 of 30.
rationale: 'Any arbitrary set of features is as good as any other' universalises beyond 27/30 datasets and tested subset sizes.

main_claim: BayesAdapter turns pretrained NNs into BNNs via Bayesian fine-tuning with low overhead and calibrated uncertainty.
evidence: Unnamed 'diverse set of challenging benchmarks': satisfactory efficiency, competitive accuracy, calibrated uncertainty.
rationale: Title attributes broadly supported. Results phrased modestly; 'to the masses' is an aspiration, not a reported result.

main_claim: ProbGAN is the first probabilistic GAN with a faithful equilibrium and outperforms multi-generator and probabilistic GANs.
evidence: Theoretical equilibrium analysis; synthetic data, CIFAR-10, STL-10, ImageNet.
rationale: 'Towards' title tentative. Superiority scoped to named datasets; 'first' tied to a specific theoretical property.

main_claim: EWoK learns robust policies by estimating the worst-case kernel, working atop any non-robust RL algorithm.
evidence: Experiments on Cartpole, MinAtar and DeepMind Control Suite.
rationale: 'Tackling' read as task description, coded 0. Named environments support claims; 'any off-the-shelf' is a design property.

main_claim: GraphNorm acts as a preconditioner, speeding GNN convergence and improving generalization over other normalizations.
evidence: Theoretical spectrum-smoothing analysis; convergence versus BatchNorm and others; graph classification benchmarks.
rationale: 'Principled' attribute backed by theory. Claims scoped to graph classification; 'much faster' unquantified but not overreach alone.

main_claim: DBSCAN-based hierarchical framework gives scalable, robust point set representations across dimensions.
evidence: Evaluations on synthetic datasets only; no numbers or baselines named.
rationale: Neutral title. Claims explicitly tied to synthetic data; 'paving the way' is forward-looking; torn none/mild, chose none.

main_claim: BOF4 quantizers reduce block-wise quantization error; with OPQ they top 4-bit block-wise methods on perplexity.
evidence: Comparisons with NF4 and AF4; theoretical and data-driven optimisation; perplexity results.
rationale: Gerund 'Improving' title implies improvement, supported. 'Top performance' explicitly scoped to 4-bit block-wise techniques and perplexity.

main_claim: A semantic loss for logical constraints gives (near-)SOTA semi-supervised classification and better structured prediction.
evidence: Semi-supervised multi-class classification; ranking and shortest-path prediction; no numbers.
rationale: Neutral title. Hedged '(near-)SOTA'; tasks named; unquantified 'significantly' alone not treated as overreach.

main_claim: RLHF on MuseD-generated multi-step deduction data significantly improves in- and out-of-domain logical reasoning.
evidence: No benchmarks, models or numbers reported; only 'significant improvements' asserted.
rationale: Gerund title implies improvement. Abstract is vague rather than clearly beyond stated evidence; rule 1 and rule 5 applied.

main_claim: Robust overfitting, robustness overestimation and the robustness-accuracy trade-off share one common cause: low-quality data.
evidence: Data-quality metric; controlled removal experiments: problems 'largely alleviated', trade-off 'less significant'; datasets unnamed.
rationale: Title supported. 'One common cause' is stronger than evidence of partial alleviation after removing low-quality samples.

main_claim: Upper and lower bounds on fairness estimation error for models trained on complete cases of incomplete data.
evidence: Theoretical bounds plus numerical experiments; 'first known results' claim.
rationale: Neutral topic title. Theory results stated; novelty qualified with 'known'.

main_claim: Batch normalization reduces adversarial and corruption robustness, via decision-boundary tilting along low-variance dimensions.
evidence: Double-digit robustness drops on five standard datasets; linear toy model and nonlinear model experiments.
rationale: Causal title ('a Cause', not 'the') backed by reported comparisons; mechanism hedged with 'we argue'.

main_claim: Skills and directed exploration emerge from simple contrastive RL given only a single goal observation.
evidence: Manipulation task example; no rewards, demonstrations or distance metrics; authors admit lacking theory.
rationale: 'All You Need' sufficiency title generalises beyond the manipulation setting described; abstract itself is measured and candid.

main_claim: Clipping off-policy tokens in SFT reduces forgetting and improves later RL; low-probability tokens primarily cause degradation.
evidence: ALFWorld and ScienceWorld: forgetting reduced 11.54%, RL performance up 7.09%; latent-space drift analysis.
rationale: Title matches results. 'Primarily results from' and 'is thus key' rest on one intervention plus correlational latent analysis.
